rationale: A wins because it is tighter and more disciplined: three real lanes, no decorative padding, and the proof gaps are named before they become lies. Its best line, "A record member payout while several stores see union drives," has conflict, timing, and a beat reporter attached. B has the sharper missed accountability thought in "REI won't say how big its resale business actually is," but it also pads with a weak "customer-story" and then repeats the same rollout as "core retail infrastructure." Good material, messier desk.
gaps_in_A: Misses the standalone sustainability-accountability angle hiding in plain sight: "the share of sales from used gear" is not just proof for the infrastructure angle, it can be the story.
Overstates motive in "the company is currently choosing not to support with a number"; the update only says the share is not disclosed, not that REI refused when asked.
The co-op dividend angle needs the actual dividend amount before it is worth pitching; A flags this correctly, but the headline still asks a reporter to care about a number it does not have.
gaps_in_B: "Story type: customer-story" is mislabeled. There is no customer, no member anecdote, and no counter experience in the facts; it is a retail-ops angle wearing a customer hat.
"REI won't say how big its resale business actually is" overreaches. The update says the share is not disclosed; "won't say" implies a refusal B has not earned.
The first and fourth angles are padded cousins: "from a pilot program to all 180+ stores" and "core retail infrastructure" are mostly the same rollout at two altitudes.
"the dividend flows to paying customer-members, not to the employees organizing" smuggles in a distinction the facts do not confirm. Useful tension, sloppy proof posture.
